body:
### Summary

## Summary

Since uv 0.12.0 stabilized the `adjust-ulimit` behavior (PR #20225), the
raised soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` is inherited by all subprocesses and breaks
tools whose startup cost scales with the open-file limit. In particular,
`tcsh` (`/bin/csh`) closes **every file descriptor from 0 to
`RLIMIT_NOFILE`** at startup, so any csh subprocess under `uv run` pays
O(RLIMIT_NOFILE) syscalls (~524k `close()` calls) and becomes ~100x slower.

This effectively makes `uv run` unusable for csh-based toolchains (e.g. the
GAMIT GNSS processing suite, which is entirely csh scripts).

## Environment

- uv: 0.12.1 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl), also reproduced reasoning applies to 0.12.0
- Linux container (Debian/Ubuntu base), image built with `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest`
- `/bin/csh` = tcsh 6.x

## Reproduction

```sh
# NOFILE before uv: soft=1024, hard=524288
python3 -c 'import resource; print(resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE))'
# (1024, 524288)

# After uv: soft raised to hard
uv run python3 -c 'import resource; print(resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE))'
# (524288, 524288)

# Time a trivial csh invocation
time uv run /bin/csh -f -c 'exit 0'        # ~0.37s
time /bin/csh -f -c 'exit 0'               # ~0.002s

# strace shows the child closing the whole fd range:
#   close(39031) close(142232) close(267235) ... close(524287)  (~524,424 calls)
```

With the limit capped, it is fast again:

```sh
ulimit -n 4096 && uv run /bin/csh -f -c 'exit 0'   # ~0.005s
```

Real-world impact: a GAMIT project-setup script (`sh_setup`) takes ~10s
under `uv run` vs ~0.14s with `ulimit -n 1024`.

## Root cause

uv 0.12.0 stabilized "Automatic open-file limit adjustment on Unix"
(#20225, originally #17464): uv raises the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` toward the
hard limit (capped at 1,048,576) at startup, and the new limit applies to
subprocesses.

`tcsh` (and `csh`) at startup iterate `close()` from 0 to `sysconf(_SC_OPEN_MAX)`
(= soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE`) to prevent leaking inherited file descriptors. With
the soft limit raised to 524288, each csh process executes ~524k `close()`
syscalls. csh-based toolchains chain many such subprocesses, so the cost
compounds.

## Expected behavior

Raising `RLIMIT_NOFILE` is fine for uv itself, but the raised soft limit
being inherited by every subprocess (`exec`ed via `uv run`) has surprising
O(limit) startup costs in otherwise-unaffected tools.

Options to consider:

- Only raise the soft limit for the uv process itself, and restore the
  original soft limit around `uv run` subprocess spawns.
- Respect an existing lower soft limit (don't raise it when the process was
  started under an already-low limit), or make the adjustment opt-out via an
  env var (e.g. `UV_NO_ULIMIT=1`).
- Cap the inherited soft limit for subprocesses lower than uv's own limit.

## Workaround (current)

Wrap `uv run` with a capped limit:

```sh
ulimit -n 4096 && exec uv run ...
```

## Note

`adjust-ulimit` was opt-in (preview) before 0.12.0, so this is a behavior
regression introduced by the 0.12.0 stabilization for any program whose
startup scales with the open-file limit.

### Platform

Linux container (Debian/Ubuntu base)

### Version

0.12.1

### Python version

3.13.6
title: adjust-ulimit (0.12.0) makes every tcsh/csh subprocess ~100x slower
